key_insight: LATHE turns natural-language materials hypotheses into differentiable geometric edits of crystal structures, enabling fine-grained constraint-based crystal manipulation rather than generating structures from scratch.
engineering_relevance: This gives materials engineers an interpretable closed-loop workflow for steering crystals toward target symmetry, bonding, and property constraints in inverse design pipelines.
method: Defines seven crystal-editing objectives: bond length, bond angle, dihedral angle, coordination environment, lattice parameters, cell volume, and space group.
Uses differentiable optimization to directly edit an input crystal while keeping the structure near local energy minima.
Exposes the toolkit through an MCP server and a multi-agent loop that converts natural-language hypotheses into executable geometric modifications.
evidence_signal: Across single-property benchmarks, LATHE achieves near-perfect satisfaction for all seven property types, and in band-gap inverse design it reaches the target window in 9/10 runs with about 13 hypothesis-evaluation cycles per run.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate objective formulation and optimization stability, so complex constraints or poor initial structures may still be sensitive to implementation details.
paper_title: LATHE: LAnguage-driven Toolkit for Hypothesis-based crystal Editing
